summary: MinSU Clearance System — iteration 1. Backend: 32/32 pytest tests passing covering auth (register/login/logout), bcrypt hash verification via direct MongoDB read, clearance create/list/process, Registrar-last-approval rule, approve-then-approved end-state, reject flow, stats (admin + student + faculty), admin users + audit-logs + actions endpoints, admin delete user, non-admin auth gating, and clearance-scoped audit-trail lifecycle. Frontend: login renders MinSU branding + campus background + feature list, admin login lands on dashboard showing Welcome header + stats cards (Total/Pending/Approved/Rejected), Users tab lists all 16 users with Delete buttons, Audit Trail tab shows 46 entries with filterable table and all expected actions (user.login, user.register, user.logout, clearance.create, clearance.approve, clearance.reject, admin.delete_user).

minor.issue: Endpoint accepts any user_id (even unknown) and returns success; audit log still writes with null actor_email. Consider 404 when user not found or reject in middleware.
allow_origins=['*'] combined with allow_credentials=True is rejected by browsers per CORS spec. Works in this app because there are no cookies, but should be tightened to explicit origin(s) from env.

issues: Status column displays the pill labels 'APPROVED'/'REJECTED' for audit log status values of 'success'/'failure' — semantically misleading since these are login/logout/action outcomes, not approvals. Consider renaming the pills to 'SUCCESS'/'FAILURE'.

action_items: (Optional) Return 404 from /api/auth/logout when user_id does not exist
(Optional) Change audit trail status pill wording from APPROVED/REJECTED to SUCCESS/FAILURE
(Optional) Restrict CORS allow_origins to explicit host instead of '*' when allow_credentials=True
critical_code_review_comments: server.py mixes concerns (auth, clearance, admin, audit, startup) in ~650 lines — acceptable now but should be split into routers/auth.py, routers/clearances.py, routers/admin.py as the app grows.

Trust model: every protected endpoint takes user_id as a query parameter rather than a signed session/JWT. Any client knowing an admin UUID can impersonate them. This is fine for a prototype but must be replaced with proper session tokens/cookies before production.
write_audit swallows exceptions silently (only logs) — good for resilience but combined with the weak auth model means a compromised endpoint could forge audit entries. Not a blocker for MVP.
Password policy is not enforced at register (no min length / complexity). Consider Pydantic validator.
No rate limiting / brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login despite audit writing failure entries.
bcrypt 4.x truncates passwords >72 bytes silently — low risk but worth documenting.
Clearance process endpoint allows ?user_id= of any faculty, but no check that the requesting user actually matches the authenticated session (same trust issue as above).
test_credentials: Admin: admin@minsu.edu.ph / Admin@MinSU2025 (auto-seeded). Test users are created inline with test_student_<runid>, test_fac_<office>_<runid> prefixes.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run registers 1 student + 6 faculty + 1 reject-flow student + 1 reject-flow faculty + 1 delete-target student per RUN_ID. Safe to re-run (unique RUN_ID). DB retains seeded data across iterations.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Default admin is idempotent via startup event. MongoDB at mongodb://localhost:27017 / db=minsu_clearance. Frontend is a vanilla JS SPA injected by /app/frontend/src/App.js loading /js/app.js and /css/style.css. The React shell only mounts once; SPA routing is internal to app.js. All 32 backend tests in /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py are self-contained and idempotent thanks to a per-run RUN_ID. Bcrypt is verified both through the API (login after register) and directly from MongoDB (password_hash starts with $2). Audit trail behavior is fully exercised end-to-end (create → 5 approvals → registrar approval → trail has 6 clearance.approve entries + 1 clearance.create).
rca of the issue: No bugs requiring RCA. One initial test fixture conflict (faculty key 'student' collided with student test email) was fixed in the test script by mapping office->explicit key.
